authorized_ref: PENDING: refs/tags/<TAG> -- the owner chooses the exact release tag name; the signer identity and stable builder id are both derived from it
note: CANONICAL SOURCE, and the EXTERNAL TRUST ROOT. An independent consumer must obtain an owner-authorized copy of this file (or its sha256) through a channel independent of the release, and pass it to verify_release.py --trusted-policy. Online verification fails closed without one: a release cannot authorize itself, because a malicious artifact can always carry a policy naming its own signer. Every PENDING must become an exact value before any signature is trusted -- enforced structurally over every leaf. A wildcard anywhere is itself a verification failure. Resolution is an act of authorization performed by a human in a reviewed commit; no automated step may perform it.
oidc_issuer: PENDING: https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com -- confirmed by identity discovery before being written here as an exact value
pinned_revision: PENDING: the 40-hex REVIEWED revision C, for traceability. Not the released commit: the released commit A is C's descendant carrying this authorization record. Content authorization is reviewed_payload_sha256, which an offline consumer can recompute; this field records history and is checked by the release workflow, which has the repository
reviewed_payload_sha256: PENDING: 64-hex digest of the reviewed release payload, excluding the authorization closure (this policy and its deterministic manifest/RO-Crate derivatives). Recomputable from the signed ZIP without a Git checkout. See payload_digest in release_trust.py
signer_identity: PENDING: derived as https://github.com/{owner}/{repo}/{workflow_path}@{authorized_ref}; must equal the certificate SAN Sigstore verifies against
trusted_builders: PENDING: github-actions://{owner}/{repo}/{workflow_path}@{authorized_ref} -- the stable builder id, derived from the same three values as signer_identity; per-run data never appears here
